title: Long-Term Care
hero.text: For patients with chronic illness, disability or prolonged recovery needs, to support stability, independence and quality of life.

overview: Some journeys of care are measured not in days, but in months or years. Long-term care at Cambridge Hospital supports patients who need continuous medical management, skilled nursing and sustained rehabilitation over an extended period - built around stability, dignity and meaningful human connection.

Every care plan is personal, every routine is intentional and every patient is treated as an individual, not a condition. Through familiar caregivers, structured daily care and active family involvement, we work to preserve dignity, maintain function and enhance quality of life, whatever the complexity of each patient’s medical needs.

blocks.text: Long-term care provides ongoing support for patients who need help with activities of daily living, such as eating, dressing, bathing and moving, alongside continuous medical and nursing care.
It is designed for patients who are medically stable but not fully independent and who benefit from a supportive, supervised environment with skilled staff available around the clock.
Unlike a short hospital stay with a defined end point, long-term care is an ongoing relationship that adapts as a patient’s needs change over time.

Patients may need long-term care for many reasons, including chronic illness, physical or cognitive disability, the lasting effects of a stroke or serious injury, or a recovery that simply needs more time.
Some patients depend on a ventilator or other medical technology, while others need support managing complex or multiple conditions on a day-to-day basis.
What they share is a need for consistent, expert care and support that may be difficult to provide at home, delivered by a team that knows them and understands their individual needs.

topics.label: A Care Plan Built Around Each Patient

blocks.text: No two patients are the same, so no two care plans are either.

Our physicians, nurses and therapists assess each patient’s medical needs, abilities and personal goals, then build a personalised care plan that is regularly reviewed and adapted as their condition and priorities change.
Familiar caregivers and predictable daily routines bring a sense of stability that matters greatly in long-term care, helping patients feel secure, understood and at home.

topics.label: Skilled Nursing and Daily Medical Support

blocks.text: At the heart of long-term care is round-the-clock skilled nursing.
Our teams manage medications, wound and skin care, nutrition and feeding, continence care and chronic conditions, helping identify changes early and address them before they become more serious.
Patients also receive hands-on support with everyday tasks that illness or disability has made difficult, always delivered with patience, respect and dignity.
Our teams have experience caring for medically complex patients, including those who depend on a ventilator to breathe.
We provide supportive, continuous respiratory and medical management for these patients and, where clinically appropriate, work towards reducing ventilator dependence over time.
Complex needs are managed with calm, specialist expertise and coordinated care, helping patients avoid unnecessary disruption and supporting greater continuity in their care.
Long-term care and rehabilitation go hand in hand.

Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, and speech and language therapy are integrated into daily life to maintain strength, mobility, communication and independence, while making the most of every gain.
Even where full recovery is not the goal, therapy can help patients remain as active, capable and comfortable as possible, for as long as possible.
